title: Reverse Hyperextension
summary: A hip extension done face down on a reverse hyper, swinging your legs up behind you for the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for hamstrings (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.5 for lower back (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Lie face down with your hips at the edge of the pad and hold the handles.
Raise your legs back and up until they line up with your body.

form_cues.cue: Raise the legs with the glutes
Let the glutes start the movement, not momentum.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
